newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton's arrival is gift for Kremlin imagemakers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton's arrival is gift for Kremlin imagemakers.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's imagemakers, struggling for months to prove he was fit to rule Russia, could not have asked for a more welcome scene at Helsinki's Vantaa airport on Thursday.
The president, in a wheelchair, was taken off the plane in a catering truck. It took a while but he eventually emerged, smiling sheepishly, his right leg stuck out awkwardly in front.
But this was not Yeltsin, 65 and with a weak heart. It was 50-year-old keen jogger Bill Clinton.

By contrast, the Kremlin leader, who earlier this year appeared unable to make the summit, looked positively nimble as he descended the steps of his sparkling new presidential plane three hours later, in bouyant mood, his wife Naina on his arm.
He smiled broadly as he was greeted by Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari and stood hatless in a freezing wind while a band played the Russian and Finnish anthems.
Clinton, on the other hand, did without a musical welcome.
"We assume it's because he is in a wheelchair and it would not be proper if he can't stand," a Finnish Foreign Ministry official said.

Yeltsin, relishing in his recent recovery from the pneumonia which followed his heart surgery, has already made the most of Clinton's fall in Florida last Friday which meant a torn tendon and emergency surgery.
"They said that a sick Yeltsin and a healthy Clinton would come to Helsinki and it turns out the other way around," the Russian leader said on Monday, a twinkle in his eye.
On the eve of the summit, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky heralded more ribbing to come over Clinton's health when the two leaders meet later on Thursday.
"I think there will be quite a few jokes on that subject," he said.
Just weeks ago, as Yeltsin battled pneumonia which came on top of quituple heart bypass surgery, the summit had looked like a major test of stamina.
But a lively performance during recent appearances means his health has slipped down the agenda. On Thursday, it was the U.S. officials who were out to show their leader was on the mend.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton began his flight to Helsinki with an onboard workout involving parallel bars and weights.
"It's a serious deal," he said. "You, like, sweat."
McCurry said the presidential plane had been slightly modified to help Clinton get around, with the doors to his cabin and office removed.

When it landed, a truck belonging to the Finnish national carrier, Finnair -- more like a compartment on a hydraulic lift -- manouevred into place alongside and was raised and lowered as Secret Service agents swarmed around.
A white van with tinted glass appeared and the U.S. president was wheeled into it and whisked off in a convoy of limousines, minibuses and an ambulance.
